profile.name: John Manuel
profile.intro: I’m John, a mechatronics student at Waterloo. I like the point in a build where a drawing, a few wires and some code finally do something together.
profile.tagline: I build things where mechanics, electronics and code meet.

projects.title: Tower of Hanoi gantry
projects.summary: A four-person first-year robot: a fixed bridge, trolley, four-bar lift and two-jaw gripper that solves a four-disc Tower of Hanoi in 15 moves.
projects.editorPrompt: Show the horizontal carriage and vertical lift. Credit teammates and identify John's part.

projects.nextStep: Capture login, a typed meal, and the parsed record from demo data only.
projects.disclaimer: A personal log for one person. It is not medical advice and it does not decide a dose.
projects.title: Insulin tracker
projects.summary: A natural-language insulin log I built for my grandmother. She types what she ate, and a language model returns dose and timing records as strict JSON.
projects.editorPrompt: TODO: three screens from a local run with made-up data, in a phone frame. Never use real health data.

projects.nextStep: Record calibration, cursor travel, and one deliberate wink-click against a normal blink.
projects.title: HeadNav
projects.summary: A free, webcam-only mouse you control with your head, with personal calibration and wink, mouth, nod or dwell clicks, for people with limited hand mobility.
projects.editorPrompt: TODO: a webcam inset with landmarks beside the cursor hitting targets. No screenshot exists yet.

goals.title: A balancing delivery robot
goals.question: Can a two-wheel robot carry an envelope across an office and stay balanced?
goals.proposedNextExperiment: Simulate balancing with a representative payload.
goals.successCriterionToSet: Choose a payload and measurable balance criterion before the first trial.

goals.title: Hands-free interaction
goals.question: How can someone tell whether their wink was detected during calibration?
goals.proposedNextExperiment: Compare two visual feedback cues during calibration.

origin.title: It started with my grandmother.
origin.body: She needed a simpler way to keep track of her insulin, so I built her an app. It was the first time something I made mattered to someone.
origin.photoPrompt: Photo: the insulin tracker on a phone, or you with your grandmother

origin.title: Then things started moving.
origin.body: RC cars taught me that code is only half the story. Motors, gears and batteries all get a vote.
origin.photoPrompt: Photo: an RC car on the bench, shell off

origin.title: Now I do it properly.
origin.body: I study Mechatronics Engineering at the University of Waterloo, where mechanics, electronics and software are one subject.
origin.photoPrompt: Photo: you on campus or in the lab
